_comment: The Sysible palette. ONE set of values, written down once.
Five surfaces render this platform -- the portal, Administration (the IdP),
the Controller, SLEP and Connect -- and each carried its own palette. They
had drifted into two families: --panel was #12161f in two of them and
#93a1b5, and Connect's green was #46a04a where everyone else wrote #43a047.
None of that is a design decision; it is five copies of one idea aging
apart. An operator moving from the portal into a console saw the surface
shift under them for no reason they could name.
The build systems cannot share a file -- the Controller is its own
repository, the portal is static CSS and the IdP inlines its stylesheet in
Python -- so each surface keeps its own copy and a test pins every copy to
this one. Same pattern as the module names in
files that cannot import each other, one fact.
Contrast is measured against --bg, and every value below is recorded with
what it measures. WCAG AA is 4.5:1 for body text and 3.0:1 for large text

One rule worth stating: text on a coloured fill is --on-accent, which is DARK. White on these fills fails WCAG AA on every one of them, and three of the five surfaces were doing it. SLEP and Connect already used dark ink; they were right.

--panel-2.note: a surface on a surface; three of five

--border.note: hairlines; the value three of the five surfaces already used

--muted.note: 7.78:1 on --bg -- the lighter of the two values in use, so secondary text stays readable

--accent.note: Sysible green. 5.73:1 on --bg as ink, and the fill colour for primary actions

--on-accent.note: text and marks drawn ON a coloured fill. WHITE FAILS AA on all three of ours -- 3.30:1 on green, 3.70:1 on red, 2.14:1 on amber. This dark ink gives 5.73, 5.11 and 8.86

--green-bright.note: healthy dots. 9.01:1 on --bg -- kept over the other value in use (#4caf5a, 6.84:1) because a status dot is the smallest thing on the screen and the one most often read at a glance

selectors._note: the Controller ships one skin and renders data-skin="brand"; its bare :root block is the retired Slate palette
